city.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.de: This nation of one main island plus a string of tiny Grenadine islands sits in the eastern Caribbean. It is known for the rumbling La Soufrière volcano, black-sand beaches, and the coral-ringed Tobago Cays.
city.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.la: sailboats anchored in the turquoise lagoon of the Tobago Cays with a sea turtle below
city.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.gr: People here speak English — just say hello with a big “Hello!” (heh-LOH).
city.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.fl: drew a flag with blue, yellow, and green stripes and three little green diamonds shaped like a V
city.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.cl: packed a snorkel to swim in a ring of tiny sandy cays surrounded by coral reefs
kept saying palm-lined coves there had starred as a hideout in pirate movies
city.Suriname.description: This is the smallest country in South America, tucked on the northern Atlantic coast. Almost all of it is thick rainforest, and its capital, Paramaribo, is famous for old wooden Dutch buildings.
city.Suriname.landmark: white wooden Dutch colonial buildings and cathedral of Paramaribo
city.Suriname.greeting: The official language is Dutch, where hello is “Hallo” (HAH-loh), but many people also say “Fa waka” in Sranan Tongo.
city.Suriname.flag: sketched a flag with green, white, and red stripes and a single yellow star in the middle
city.Suriname.clue.0: packed a bag for the smallest country on the whole continent of South America
city.Suriname.clue.1: hoped to watch giant leatherback turtles crawl ashore to lay eggs on quiet beaches
city.Trinidad and Tobago.description: These twin islands are the southernmost in the Caribbean, sitting just off the coast of Venezuela. They are the birthplace of steelpan drums and famous for a giant, colorful Carnival and flocks of scarlet ibis.
city.Trinidad and Tobago.landmark: flocks of bright scarlet ibis flying over the Caroni Swamp at sunset
city.Trinidad and Tobago.greeting: People here speak English — greet a friend with a cheerful “Hello!” (heh-LOH).
city.Trinidad and Tobago.flag: red, with a black diagonal stripe edged in white
city.Trinidad and Tobago.clue.0: circled two little islands right at the bottom of the Caribbean, close to South America
city.Trinidad and Tobago.clue.1: couldn't wait to dance at a huge, colorful Carnival full of feathers and costumes
city.Uruguay.description: This small country sits on South America's Atlantic coast between Brazil and Argentina. Known for wide grassy plains, cattle ranches, and sandy beaches, it is the birthplace of tango music and a towering steak sandwich called the chivito.
city.Uruguay.landmark: giant sculpted hand (Los Dedos) rising from the sand at Punta del Este beach
city.Uruguay.greeting: People speak Spanish here, so say hello with “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Uruguay.flag: pinned on a flag badge: blue and white stripes with a golden smiling sun in the corner
city.Uruguay.clue.0: studied a map of a small country squeezed between Brazil and Argentina on the Atlantic coast
city.Uruguay.clue.1: joked about visiting a land with far more cattle than people, grazing on endless grassy plains
city.Venezuela.description: This country sits on the northern coast of South America. It is home to Angel Falls, the tallest waterfall on Earth, plus the grassy Llanos plains where capybaras, caimans, and anacondas live.
city.Venezuela.landmark: Angel Falls plunging from the top of a flat-topped tepui mountain into misty jungle
city.Venezuela.greeting: People speak Spanish here, so greet someone with “Hola” (OH-lah).
city.Venezuela.flag: traced a flag: yellow, blue, and red stripes topped with an arc of white stars
